final.title: Canonical records before you automate a workflow
final.body:
If you want to automate a workflow, start with one design constraint: decide which record is canonical. In plain English, that means naming the single source of truth for one repeating process, such as customer details, invoices, orders, or support tickets, and then checking where the other tools drift away from it.

That sounds obvious until you have three versions of the same field and nobody trusts any of them. The practical question is not “can AI do this?” but “what happens when two systems disagree?” If the answer is re-keying, re-checking, or waiting for the owner to approve the same thing twice, you probably have a record-control problem before you have an automation problem.

A bounded next step is to map one workflow on paper: list the manual entry points, mark which tool currently owns each field, and note where decisions stop because the records do not match. Then separate the issue into technical and organisational parts. Technical means format, API limits, or tool behaviour. Organisational means approval chains, data ownership, or human review gates. The fix is different in each case.

If the inputs are mostly text, extraction and verification may be worth testing. If the records are already structured and synced, AI is probably not the first lever. Keep the owner in the approval loop either way, especially for money movement or other high-risk decisions.

The build stays technical; the approval stays human.
